Subject: Dedicated capacity for production inference (initial ask)

Karthik,

Hope you’re well — quick intro: I’m Tim (ops lead) at CascadeGen. We’re evaluating dedicated GPU reservations to serve our new text-generation pipeline (low-latency chat and batched embeddings for search). Traffic will be spiky (demo windows, nightly bulk jobs) and we care about predictable p99 latency under 300ms for chat.

Can you send a few realistic reservation options (cluster size, minimum guaranteed GPUs / "floor", and a ramp schedule we could include in procurement) and a sense of burst/overflow behavior? I attached a small traffic sample.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Tim Cho
Head of Platform Ops, CascadeGen

Tim — thanks for the traffic sample. Below are three reservation options we typically propose for workloads like yours. Each option includes: cluster size (GPUs), minimum guaranteed GPUs (floor), estimated steady-state cost signal, and a recommended ramp schedule. We also note burst handling and canary guidance.

1) Conservative Starter
- Cluster: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (single pool)
- Minimum guaranteed (floor): 2 GPUs
- Ramp: 2 GPUs (wk0) -> 4 GPUs (wk4) -> evaluate at wk8
- Bursts: On-demand burst allowed up to additional 2 GPUs subject to short-term capacity; preemptible for non-critical batches.
- When to pick: tight procurement constraints, need quick validation; p99 may be ~350–450ms at peak chat concurrency.

2) Production Baseline (recommended)
- Cluster: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (3 nodes of 4 GPUs)
- Minimum guaranteed (floor): 4 GPUs (keeps latency SLO stable during normal peaks)
- Ramp: 4 GPUs (wk0) -> 8 GPUs (wk3) -> 12 GPUs (wk6)
- Bursts: Guaranteed autoscale buffer of 4 GPUs for 30-minute windows; fallback routing to smaller models or hosted pool if sustained.
- When to pick: predictable latency and headroom for demo spikes; best balance of cost vs p99 latency (~220–300ms).

3) Aggressive Throughput (for larger expansion)
- Cluster: 24x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum guaranteed (floor): 8 GPUs
- Ramp: 8 GPUs (wk0) -> 16 GPUs (wk4) -> 24 GPUs (wk10)
- Bursts: Dedicated burst lane and cross-region failover for capacity.
- When to pick: sustained high request volumes and embedding backfills; lowest token cost.

Canary & rollout notes: we recommend a canary lane (1 GPU equivalent) with mirrored traffic and a staged traffic shift over 48–72 hours before full cutover. Metrics to watch: p99 latency, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, and token burn.

I’ve attached a short SOW draft and included LAUREN (solutions) to align on onboarding cadence. If you prefer, we can add a staircase commitment that smooths monthly burn.

Next steps: let me know which option you prefer and we’ll return a priced SOW with activation windows, activation SLA, and a detailed ramp calendar.

Karthik / Marcus — quick notes from infra side after reviewing the traffic profile.

- Floor guidance: floor=4 on a 12-GPU cluster is reasonable for maintaining p99 latency under normal peaks provided: (a) we reserve 1 GPU for canary + health checks, (b) models are compiled/quantized to the chosen kernels, and (c) KV cache persistence is enabled between requests.
- Warmup: plan ~6–12 hours of warm traffic for KV priming for catalog queries and chat contexts. If they expect same-day demos with cold models, bump initial floor to 6 for the first 48 hours.
- Placement: put embeddings jobs on a dedicated queue scoped to 2 GPUs to avoid blocking chat lanes; use dynamic batching with a max batch latency target of 20ms.
- Autoscale & burst: allow a 4-GPU burst window for short spikes (<= 30 minutes). For sustained overflow, route to Redwood hosted pool with an explicit agreement on fallthrough costs.

I’ll prepare a short ops-runbook snippet we can attach to the SOW describing warmup steps and health checks.

— Neha Kapoor
Infra Lead, Inference Runtime, Redwood Inference

Recommended proposal (Production Baseline)
- Cluster: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (3 nodes of 4 GPUs)
- Minimum guaranteed (floor): 4 GPUs (increase to 6 for first 48 hours if you need same-day demos)
- Ramp schedule: 4 GPUs (activation wk0) -> 8 GPUs (wk3) -> 12 GPUs (wk6)
- Canary: 1-GPU mirrored canary for 48–72h; gradual traffic shift over 48h
- Burst: 4-GPU autoscale buffer for up to 30 minutes; sustained overflow routed to hosted pool with pre-negotiated fallback costs
- Ops runbook: warmup window 6–12 hours for KV cache priming; embeddings on a 2-GPU dedicated queue

Attached: updated SOW (pricing TBD, includes activation SLA, onboarding milestones, and sample runbook). If you’re good with this, Marcus will add staircase/commit options and a monthly burn smoothing proposal. We can schedule a 30-minute sync to finalize numbers and signatures.
